science.qualification: Photosphere color from a blackbody at the star's published temperature, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret (2017), A&A 600, A30 computes from PHOENIX model atmospheres for the TESS band at 3,240 K and log g 4.82 (u1 0.158, u2 0.468): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Aug 2005
science.description: Radial component of the star's large-scale magnetic field, fitted with ZDIpy to 64 ESPaDOnS spectra of 19 August 2005 to 23 August 2005 (reduced chi-square 1.25, against 1.9 with no field); mean field 498 G. A reduction made in this project, not a published map. Black line: 70 degrees south, below which the star never faces us.

science.label: Sector 15
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 11.5 hours, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 15 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 2.3%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.80%, the light's own noise being 0.21%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 0.48 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.76, a width of 0.50 and a fit of 0.99, and in all 2 of the star's sectors together a period of 0.48 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.75, a width of 0.50 and a fit of 0.99; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 70°. Gaia DR3 lists 15 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 3.2% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 15

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffbf7c, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 56 (September 2022): the map's scale, 99% to 101% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 1.7% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · September 2022
